title: Letter sounds

parent.learn: Each letter has a name and a sound: the letter B is called “bee” but says /b/.
parent.why: We read by sounds, not names. c-a-t read by names is “see-ay-tee”; read by sounds it is /k/-/a/-/t/ — “cat”.

parent.learn: Hear the first sound of a word: “ball” starts with /b/.
parent.why: Picking out the first sound is the first step to spelling and reading a whole word.

parent.learn: Then the last sound, then the middle.
parent.why: The middle (a vowel) is the hardest to hear; the child is ready for it once first and last sounds are easy.
Stretching makes each sound separate, so the child can hear all of them.

ask: What sound does your name start with?
I spy with my little eye something starting with /m/…
Find three things in the kitchen that start with /p/.
What is the last sound in “cat”?

rounds.t: Which picture starts with the sound of b?
rounds.h: Say them: b-b-ball. Ball starts with /b/.

rounds.t: Which picture starts with the sound of c, like in cat?
rounds.h: c-c-car. Car starts with the same sound as cat.

rounds.t: Which picture starts with the sound of s?
Which picture starts with the sound of m?
Which picture starts with the sound of t?
Which word starts with the same sound as dog?
Which word starts with the same sound as snake?
Which word ends with the sound t?
rounds.h: Stretch it: c-a-t. The last sound is /t/.

rounds.t: Which word ends with the sound n?
rounds.h: Stretch it: s-u-n. The last sound is /n/.

rounds.t: What is the middle sound in cat?
rounds.h: Stretch it slowly: c-aaa-t. The middle sound is /a/.
